quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is true?

options.text: Never put an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
An airbag can hurt an infant or small child, even in a slow crash.
Make sure all passengers wear a seat belt or use a child restraint.

questions.explanation: Before driving, fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash. Children age 12 and under must sit properly restrained in the back seat. Never put a rear-facing infant restraint in the front seat of a vehicle with a front airbag.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It improves driving skills but harms judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It does not affect driving skills or judgment.
It harms judgment but not driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms many driving skills. It slows your reaction time and makes it hard to see clearly. It also affects your judgment about speed and distance. Alcohol lowers your inhibitions and makes you more likely to take dangerous risks.

questions.question: You must signal before turning, changing lanes, or leaving a curb because:

options.text: It is only needed when other traffic is nearby.
It is a good habit and the law requires it.
It is only needed during the move, not before.
It is not needed if you drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a good habit and the law requires it.
questions.explanation: Signal your intentions well before changing lanes or turning. The law requires you to signal at least 100 feet before moving your vehicle left or right. Always signal before pulling away from a curb to warn other drivers.

questions.question: Alcohol:
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your brain activity and reduces the skills you need to drive safely. Alcohol slows your reaction time and impairs your judgment.

questions.question: On a long trip, the best way to prevent driver fatigue is to:

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Switch feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop for a short break every two hours to prevent fatigue on long trips. If you feel drowsy, leave the road and park in a safe place to nap, or find a place to stay for the night.

questions.question: What happens when you mix alcohol with drugs?

options.text: The effects of both are reduced.
The effects of both are increased.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both are increased.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can increase the effects of both. It is unsafe to drive after using either alcohol or drugs. It is even more dangerous to mix them together.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.
Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines in damaged vehicles.

questions.explanation: Stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes because another vehicle could hit you. Turn off the engines in damaged vehicles.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, you should:

options.text: Continue to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, do not back up. Go to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a freeway or shoulder is illegal.

questions.question: You must always signal when:

options.text: Parking or leaving a parking space.
Entering traffic from an alley or parking area.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, parking or leaving a parking space, or entering traffic from an alley or parking area. This tells other drivers what you plan to do and helps prevent accidents.

questions.question: This shape and color sign means:
questions.explanation: A pennant-shaped sign means no passing zone.

questions.question: When you see other drivers acting or reacting in anger, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, stay away from them. Don't look at them or make gestures that could anger them more. Slow down, move away, or do whatever you can to stay safe.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull over to the side of the road and stop.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head quickly to look for other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check both mirrors to see traffic behind you. Then look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot before moving into the other lane.

questions.question: A steady yellow light means:

options.text: The light is changing from green to red.
The car ahead is going too slow.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is changing from green to red.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the light is about to turn red. Slow down and stop unless you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that a stop sign is coming. Get ready to stop completely.

questions.question: If you miss your freeway exit, you should:

options.text: Make a U-turn across the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
Find a police officer to help you get back.

questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, take the next one. Do not stop, back up, or cross the median on a highway. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a school crossing is ahead.

questions.question: A seat belt should fit:

options.text: Snugly across your hip bones and lower belly.
Tight enough to turn off the warning light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snugly across your hip bones and lower belly.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower belly. The shoulder belt should be comfortable so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:

options.text: Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show they are wrong.
Do something aggressive back to them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and get away from them. Don't try to get even, as this makes the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: Signs of a drunk driver include:
questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include weaving between lanes, speeding, driving too slowly, jerky movements, and sudden stops.

questions.question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you move your vehicle. This includes turning, changing lanes, and pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: An intersection has no traffic signs or signals. You arrive at the same time as a vehicle to your right. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and drive through the intersection.
Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
Drive through and make the other vehicle stop.
Honk your horn and drive through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way when two vehicles arrive at the same time. Let that vehicle pass first, then you may proceed.

questions.question: What should you do if you are in a serious crash?
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle and move it off the road if possible. Check for injuries. Call 911 if anyone is hurt. You must report the crash to police if there is an injury, death, or property damage over $1,000 (or over $200 in damage to government property like signs or guardrails).

questions.question: What should you do when driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and let them cross. Be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: You are angry after a work incident. When you get to your car, what should you do?

options.text: Play loud radio so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the interstate to let off steam.
Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Stop at a bar and have drinks before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: Wait until you feel calm before you drive. Driving while angry or upset is dangerous for you and others on the road.
